title: Addressable Architectural Lighting Controllers
text_faithful: Faith interpretation: Revelation 21:23-25 pictures a city whose light needs no sun or moon and whose gates never shut by day, with no night there. That picture is the design brief for radiant-city lighting; it is not, by itself, evidence that any particular control system achieves it.
engineering: An addressable controller gives every luminaire or group its own address on a control bus, so brightness, colour, and scene membership can be set per fixture instead of per circuit.
body: A Signature-original controller follows the same addressed model with its own addressing scheme and command set, built as close as possible to the public DALI-2 and DMX512-A behaviour. It is labeled Signature-original wherever its command set departs from a published standard, and it is never presented as a certified DALI or DMX product. Its value is the same discipline: one address per fixture, one recorded map, and scenes stored in the controller rather than improvised at the switch.

demo.code:
# Addressable Architectural Lighting Controllers
import math
fixtures = 96
channels_per_fixture = 4
total_channels = fixtures * channels_per_fixture
print("Fixtures addressed: %s" % (fixtures,))
print("Total control channels: %s" % (total_channels,))
print("DMX universes at 512 channels each: %s" % (math.ceil(total_channels / 512),))
demo.expected_output:
Fixtures addressed: 96
Total control channels: 384
DMX universes at 512 channels each: 1

engineering: A light-control network is the wiring, switches, gateways, and addressing plan that lets many controllers act as one system instead of many isolated panels.
body: The Signature-original network mirrors that layering with its own gateway design and its own segment documentation, approximating the public DALI, KNX, and sACN behaviour. The discipline it keeps is the public one: documented segments, spare capacity, supervised nodes, and a defined fallback for every lost link.

engineering: Reference modes are named operating states — daylight reference, dusk reference, night reference — that the control system can be measured against, so 'too bright' and 'too dim' stop being matters of opinion.

title: Adaptive Brightness Controller
text_faithful: Faith interpretation: Revelation 21:23-25 pictures a city whose light needs no sun or moon and whose gates never shut by day, with no night there. That picture is the design brief for radiant-city lighting; it is not, by itself, evidence that any particular control system achieves it.
engineering: An adaptive brightness controller adjusts output continuously in response to measured conditions, instead of holding one fixed level all night.
body: The Signature-original adaptive controller uses the same bounded structure — sensor inputs, target, minimum, maximum, and rate limit — with its own tuning tables, approximating public adaptive practice. Its bounds are stated on every zone record, and any zone whose sensor has failed is reported as running on its fallback level, never as adapting. Adaptation without stated bounds is not accepted, in either edition.

demo.code:
# Adaptive Brightness Controller
import math
target_lux = 200
measured_lux = 240
dim_step_pct = 5
correction_pct = (measured_lux - target_lux) / target_lux * 100
print("Target in lux: %s" % (target_lux,))
print("Measured in lux: %s" % (measured_lux,))
print("Excess above target in percent: %s" % (round(correction_pct, 1),))
print("Dim steps of 5 percent to correct: %s" % (math.ceil(correction_pct / dim_step_pct),))
demo.expected_output:
Target in lux: 200
Measured in lux: 240
Excess above target in percent: 20.0
Dim steps of 5 percent to correct: 4

title: Sensor-Loop Light Feedback
text_faithful: Faith interpretation: Revelation 21:23-25 pictures a city whose light needs no sun or moon and whose gates never shut by day, with no night there. That picture is the design brief for radiant-city lighting; it is not, by itself, evidence that any particular control system achieves it.
engineering: Sensor-loop feedback closes the loop: a light sensor measures what the controlled lights actually produce, and the controller corrects the difference between measured and target.
body: The Signature-original feedback loop uses the same structure — surface-facing sensor, fixed interval, dead band, and bounded gain — with its own loop record format, approximating public feedback practice. Its dead band and gain are stated per loop, and a loop whose sensor faces its own luminaire is rejected as a measurement error, in either edition.

demo.code:
# Sensor-Loop Light Feedback
target_lux = 200
measured_lux = 192
dead_band_lux = 10
error_lux = target_lux - measured_lux
print("Target in lux: %s" % (target_lux,))
print("Measured in lux: %s" % (measured_lux,))
print("Error in lux: %s" % (error_lux,))
print("Dead band in lux: %s" % (dead_band_lux,))
print("Correction required (error exceeds dead band): %s" % (error_lux > dead_band_lux,))
demo.expected_output:
Target in lux: 200
Measured in lux: 192
Error in lux: 8
Dead band in lux: 10
Correction required (error exceeds dead band): False

title: Brightness Uniformity Controller
text_faithful: Faith interpretation: Revelation 21:23-25 pictures a city whose light needs no sun or moon and whose gates never shut by day, with no night there. engineering: A uniformity controller keeps brightness even across a surface or a street, so no patch glares while its neighbour sits dim.
body: The Signature-original uniformity controller uses the same grid, ratio, and trimming method with its own grid record, approximating public uniformity practice. Its target ratio is stated per surface, and a surface whose grid was measured at a different height than its design grid is re-measured, not assumed. Uniformity claimed from one sensor is not uniformity, in either edition.

demo.code:

lux_values_sum = 1800
min_lux = 170
avg_lux = lux_values_sum / points
print("Grid points: %s" % (points,))
print("Average in lux: %s" % (avg_lux,))
print("Minimum in lux: %s" % (min_lux,))
print("Uniformity minimum-to-average: %s" % (round(min_lux / avg_lux, 3),))
demo.expected_output:
Grid points: 9
Average in lux: 200.0
Minimum in lux: 170
Uniformity minimum-to-average: 0.85
